chapter_seo_title: Bone Buddha Temple: Li Huowang Faces a Mute Monk and a Deadly Dilemma | Dao Gui Yi Xian
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang and the team enter the Bone Buddha Temple. A silent monk with telepathy is their only defense as they hunt the Zuowandao master Facai. But even fail-safes can fail.
og_title: Bone Buddha Temple: The Temple of Relics and Ruin
og_description: A new mission begins. Touching down at a temple built around a mummified Buddha, Li Huowang faces Zuowandao's Facai. But the real danger might be the cold logic of a kill order.
twitter_title: Chapter 336: Enter the Temple of Flesh and Bones
twitter_description: Li Huowang is sent on a mission with a quiet monk and a golden abacus. The rules for surviving Zuowandao just got a little bit bloodier.

lore_anchors.definition: A Buddhist monk's preserved body, venerated as a living relic after death. In the Dao-Twisted World, such mummies are enshrined in temples, but their twisted, dried-out appearance carries a ghoulish overtone.
A Buddhist ascetic practice of renouncing speech to achieve spiritual discipline. Chan Master Xinchi uses this to remain immune to Zuowandao's verbal tricks.
One of the Six Supernatural Powers in Buddhism; the ability to read or communicate with the mind of another. Here, it allows the mute monk to issue commands directly into Li Huowang's thoughts.
The three highest-ranking members of Zuowandao. Facai (发财, "Get Rich") is confirmed as one of them, positioning her as an elite adversary alongside the mysterious North Wind (北风).

A high-ranking eunuch official of the Supervisory Heavenly Office. He exudes the powdered, theatrical authority of a Ming court official, one who mixes bureaucratic grandeur with a faint air of physical decay.

Literally "Get Rich," one of Zuowandao's Three Elements. A master manipulator whose words are a labyrinth of traps. The Chief Recorder's survival tactic: believe three-tenths, doubt three-tenths, and ignore three-tenths.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Bone Buddha Temple?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A temple in Langzhong City that enshrines a "Flesh-Bone Bodhisattva"—a mummified monk venerated as a living Buddha. It has been compromised by Zuowandao.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can't Facai trick Chan Master Xinchi?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because Xinchi cultivates the Vow of Silence (闭口禅), he does not speak. Since he cannot be drawn into a verbal exchange, Facai's lies and illusions cannot take hold of him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the civilian Li Huowang killed actually a Zuowandao?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. Chan Master Xinchi admitted he "made a mistake." This suggests that even with perfect immunity to deception, discerning the enemy's identity is fraught with risk.
